description:
I'm holding this metal Slinky right in the palm of my hand — I let the bottom drop, and it bounces. Was it the hand, or the spring?

Thinking in Systems by Donella H. Meadows, explained: why the problems that refuse to stay fixed — traffic, debt, burnout, collapsing fisheries — are not caused by stupid or evil people, but by the structure we keep ignoring. We walk through stocks and flows (the bathtub), balancing and reinforcing feedback loops (the thermostat and the shoving match), delays (the car dealer and the hotel shower), renewable vs. non-renewable limits (the Newfoundland cod collapse), resilience and hierarchy, the system traps (success to the successful, shifting the burden), and Meadows' leverage points — from the tiny dial everyone twists to the paradigm lever nobody wants to touch. Then we take on the hardest objection: is "it's the system" just a cop-out?
